story.short_summary: Sammy the snake is very short and feels sad because it cannot reach the fruit on a high branch. Sammy asks the children for help, so [TEACHER NAME] and the children each build their own super long LEGO snake to show Sammy how long a snake can be.
story.call_and_response_note: Children repeat the key phrase chorally each time Sammy slithers across the story.
story.full_story_speaker_notes: Teacher gathers the children and shows Sammy the Snake stretching toward a piece of fruit on a branch, but Sammy is too short to reach. Teacher: 'Oh no, poor Sammy is too short to reach the fruit! Sammy wishes it could be longer.' Children guess how Sammy feels. Teacher: 'Let's say hello to Sammy first: Sss, sss, slither with me!' Children repeat chorally, wiggling like a snake. Teacher: 'Let's look closely at Sammy. What color is Sammy? Is Sammy's body long or short? Does Sammy have legs?' Teacher points out the long body, the pattern on the skin, and the small head, letting children observe. Teacher: 'I have an idea! Sammy is asking all of us for help. Since none of us can make Sammy longer, what if each of YOU builds your very own LEGO snake, as long as you can make it, so Sammy has lots of long snake friends?' Children cheer. Teacher: 'Today, each of us is going to build our own very long LEGO snake!'
